en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Tikadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (4) 4.5.
The Wholesome Triplet, the Great Intermediate Dyad Group on Grasping.
4.5.1. The Triplet of the Wholesome, the Pair of Having an Object, and the Tetrad of Conditions:
Dependent on a wholesome state that has an object, a wholesome state that has an object arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome state with an object, an unwholesome state with an object arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate state with an object, an indeterminate state with an object arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are three;
under object condition there are three ... pe ... under resultant condition there is one ... pe ... under non-disappearance condition there are three. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on "Co-nascent" and "Associated" are also similar to the section on "Dependent. Root-object:
A wholesome state with an object is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome state with an object.
An unwholesome state with an object is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome state with an object.
An indeterminate state with an object is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an indeterminate state with an object.
A wholesome state with an object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome state with an object. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to root: three; with respect to object: nine; with respect to predominance: seven; with respect to proximity: seven ... pe ...

with respect to conascence, mutuality, and support: three; with respect to decisive support: nine; with respect to repetition: three; with respect to kamma: five; with respect to result: one; with respect to nutriment ... pe ... with respect to association:
three ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance: three. (Abbreviated.)
(As in the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so it should be expanded in detail.
Dependent on an indeterminate state that is without an object, an indeterminate state without an object arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)
Under the root condition: one [answer] …pe… under the non-disappearance condition: one. (Abbreviated. Under the not-root condition: one …pe… under the not-disappearance condition: one. (Abbreviated.
(The "Conascent" chapter …pe… and the "Associated" chapter are also the same as the "Dependent" chapter.)
An indeterminate (abyākata) state without an object-condition (anārammaṇa) is a condition for an indeterminate state without an object-condition by way of:
conascence-condition (sahajāta-paccaya), mutuality-condition (aññamañña-paccaya), dependence-condition (nissaya-paccaya), nutriment-condition (āhāra-paccaya),
faculty-condition (indriya-paccaya), presence-condition (atthi-paccaya), and non-disappearance-condition (avigata-paccaya).
(All cases are the same. Abbreviated. 4.5.2.
The Triplet on the Wholesome, the Dyad on Consciousness, and the Tetrad on Conditions.
A wholesome state of consciousness is a condition for a wholesome state of consciousness by way of object-condition.

(Abbreviated. Nine in the case of object; seven in the case of predominance; seven in the case of proximity … pe … nine in the case of decisive support; three in the case of repetition; seven in the case of absence;
seven in the case of disappearance. (Abbreviated. Nine in the case of not-root; nine in the case of not-object. (Abbreviated.)
(As in the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so it should be expanded in detail:
Dependent on a wholesome state that is not mental, a wholesome state that is not mental arises by way of root condition... three.
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is not mental, an unwholesome state that is not mental arises by way of root condition... three.
Dependent on an indeterminate, non-mental state, an indeterminate, non-mental state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both a wholesome, non-mental state and an indeterminate, non-mental state, an indeterminate, non-mental state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both an unwholesome, non-mental state and an indeterminate, non-mental state, an indeterminate, non-mental state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome, non-conscious state, a wholesome, non-conscious state arises by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are nine;
under object-condition there are three; under predominance-condition there are nine … pe … under result-condition there is one … pe … under non-disappearance-condition there are nine.
A wholesome, non-conscious state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome, non-conscious state. (Abbreviated.)
In the root condition, seven; in the object condition, nine; in the predominance condition, ten … pe … in the non-disappearance condition, thirteen. (Abbreviated.
4.5.3. The Wholesome Triplet, the Mental Factor Dyad, and the Fourfold Condition Set.
Dependent on a wholesome mental state, a wholesome mental state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome mental state, an unwholesome mental state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate mental state, an indeterminate mental state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to root-condition: three; with respect to object-condition: three ... pe ... with respect to result-condition: one ... pe ...
with respect to non-disappearance-condition: three. (Abbreviated. (The "Conascent" section ... pe ... and the "Associated" section are also like the "Dependent" section. Root-object.
A wholesome mental state is a condition for a wholesome mental state by way of the root-condition.
An unwholesome mental state is a condition for an unwholesome mental state by way of the root-condition.
A neutral mental state is a condition for a neutral mental state by way of the root-condition.
A wholesome mental state is a condition for a wholesome mental state by way of object-condition … three.
An unwholesome mental state is a condition for an unwholesome mental state by way of object-condition … three.
A neutral mental state is a condition for a neutral mental state by way of object-condition … three. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to cause: three; with respect to object: nine; with respect to predominance: seven; with respect to proximity: seven ... [and so on] ...

with respect to conascence, mutuality, and dependence: three; with respect to strong-dependence: nine; with respect to repetition: three; with respect to kamma: five; with respect to result: one; with respect to nutriment ...
[and so on] ... with respect to association: three ... [and so on] ... with respect to non-disappearance: three. (Abbreviated.)
(As in the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so it should be expanded in detail:
Dependent upon a wholesome non-mental state, a neutral non-mental state arises by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent upon an unwholesome non-mental state, a neutral non-mental state arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate, non-mental state, an indeterminate, non-mental state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both a wholesome, non-mental state and an indeterminate, non-mental state, an indeterminate, non-mental state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both an unwholesome, non-mental state and an indeterminate, non-mental state, an indeterminate, non-mental state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
Under the root condition, five; under the object condition, one ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition, five.
Under the not-root condition, one; under the not-object condition, five; under the not-disappearance condition, five.
(The "Conascent" chapter and the "Investigation" chapter should also be expanded in this manner.)
4.5.4. The Wholesome Triplet, the Couplets on Mental Association, etc.

Dependent on a wholesome state associated with consciousness … dependent on a wholesome state conjoined with consciousness … dependent on a wholesome state originated by consciousness … dependent on a wholesome state coexistent with consciousness … [and so forth].
Dependent on ... [and so forth] ... dependent on wholesome states that follow the mind; ... dependent on wholesome states that are conjoined with and produced by the mind; ...
dependent on wholesome states that are conjoined with, produced by, and co-existent with the mind; ...
dependent on wholesome states that are conjoined with, produced by, and follow the mind, there arises a wholesome state that is conjoined with, produced by, and follows the mind.
A state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Three under root; three under object … pe … one under result … pe … three under non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
(The sections on conascent, associated, and inquiry should also be expanded in this manner.)
4.5.5. The Tetrad on Conditions in the Wholesome Triplet, the Internal Dyad:
Dependent on an indeterminate internal state, an indeterminate internal state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition, one; in the case of conascence, one ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance, one.
(Abbreviated. (The section on conascence ... pe ... and the section on association are similar to the section on dependence.
A wholesome internal state is a condition for a wholesome internal state by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).
A wholesome internal state is a condition for an unwholesome internal state by way of object-condition.
A wholesome internal state is a condition for an indeterminate internal state by way of object-condition.
An unwholesome internal state is a condition for an unwholesome internal state by way of object-condition … three [cases].
An internal indeterminate state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an internal indeterminate state... three. (Abbreviated. Nine in the case of the object; ... dominance ...
seven in the case of immediate succession; one in the case of conascence, dependence, and support; nine in the case of decisive support; three in the case of prenascence;
one in the case of postnascence; three in the case of repetition; one in the case of resultant, nutriment, and faculty... etc.
With dissociation, three; ... pe ... with non-disappearance, five. (Abbreviated.
[As the section on questions in the *Kusala-ttika*, so it should be expanded.
Dependent on an external wholesome state, an external wholesome state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root-cause, nine; in the case of object, three ... pe ... in the case of resultant, one ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance, nine.
An external wholesome state is a condition, by way of root-cause condition, for an external wholesome state.
(Abbreviated. In the case of root-cause, seven; in the case of object, nine ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance, thirteen. (Abbreviated.)
(As in the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so it should be expanded in detail.
4.5.6. *Kusalattika*, *Upādāduka*, and the Tetrad of Conditions.
A neutral derived phenomenon is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for a neutral derived phenomenon; ... by way of faculty-condition; ... by way of presence-condition; ...
by way of non-disappearance-condition. [In the case of nutriment there is one; in the case of faculty, presence, and non-disappearance there is one. (Abbreviated.
Dependent on a wholesome non-derived phenomenon, a wholesome non-derived phenomenon arises by way of root-condition; ... three.
Dependent on an unwholesome non-clinging state, an unwholesome non-clinging state arises by way of root condition... three [cases].
Dependent on an indeterminate non-clinging state, an indeterminate non-clinging state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both a wholesome non-clinging state and an indeterminate non-clinging state, an indeterminate non-clinging state arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on unwholesome and non-clinging, and indeterminate and non-clinging states, arises an indeterminate and non-clinging state by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are nine;
under object condition there are three … pe … under result condition there is one … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are nine. (Abbreviated.
The section on co-nascence … pe … and the section on association are the same as the section on dependence.
A wholesome state that is not derived is related to a wholesome state that is not derived by way of the root condition ... three.
An unwholesome state that is not derived is related to an unwholesome state that is not derived by way of the root condition ... three.
A neutral state that is not derived is related to a neutral state that is not derived by way of the root condition.
A wholesome non-clinging state is related to a wholesome non-clinging state by way of object condition ... three.
An unwholesome non-clinging state is related to an unwholesome non-clinging state by way of object condition ... three.
An indeterminate non-clinging state is related to an indeterminate non-clinging state by way of object condition ... three. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root condition, there are seven; in object condition, nine; in predominance condition, ten; in proximity ... [etc. ... in conascence condition, seven; in mutuality condition, three; in dependence and strong-dependence conditions, nine ... [etc. ... in dissociation condition, three ... [etc. ... in non-disappearance condition, eleven. (Abbreviated.
(As the section on questions in the Wholesome Triplet, so it should be expanded.
4.5.7. The Wholesome Triplet, the Clung-to Dyad.
The Tetrad of Conditions:
Dependent on a neutral (*abyākata*) state that is clung-to (*upādinna*), a neutral state that is clung-to arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
(Abbreviated. Under the root condition there is one; under the object condition (*ārammaṇa*) there is one ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*) there is one. (Abbreviated.)
(In the section on co-nascence ... pe ... and in the section on inquiry, it is the same everywhere.
Dependent on a wholesome state not acquired by clinging, a wholesome state not acquired by clinging arises by way of root condition ... three.
Dependent on an unwholesome state not acquired by clinging, an unwholesome state not acquired by clinging arises by way of root condition ... three.
Dependent on a neutral (abyākata) and non-clung-to (anupādinna) state, a neutral and non-clung-to state arises by way of root condition (hetupaccaya).
Dependent on both a wholesome (kusala) and non-clung-to state and a neutral and non-clung-to state, a neutral and non-clung-to state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both an unwholesome (akusala) and non-clung-to state and a neutral and non-clung-to state, a neutral and non-clung-to state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root-condition, nine; in the case of object-condition, three ... pe ... in the case of resultant-condition, one ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance-condition, nine.
(Abbreviated. (The section on co-nascence ... pe ... and the section on association are the same as the section on dependence. Root-object.
A wholesome state not acquired by clinging is related to a wholesome state not acquired by clinging by way of root condition … three.
An unwholesome state not acquired by clinging is related to an unwholesome state not acquired by clinging by way of root condition … three.
A neutral state not acquired by clinging is related to a neutral state not acquired by clinging by way of root condition.
A wholesome state not acquired by clinging is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome state not acquired by clinging … three.
An unwholesome state not acquired by clinging is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome state not acquired by clinging … three.
A neutral state not acquired by clinging is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a neutral state not acquired by clinging … [three].
Condition. An indeterminate, non-clung-to state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome, non-clung-to state.
An indeterminate, non-clung-to state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome, non-clung-to state.
… three. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to root-condition: seven; object-condition: nine; predominance-condition: ten; proximity-condition: six … pe … conascence-condition:
nine; mutuality-condition: three; dependence-condition: nine; strong-dependence-condition: nine; prenascence, postnascence, and repetition-conditions: three … pe … dissociation-condition:
three … pe … non-disappearance-condition: eleven. (Abbreviated.)
The Great Intermediate Dyads on the Wholesome Triplet are finished.
4.5.8. The Wholesome Triplet, the Clinging Dyads, etc.
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is subject to clinging, an unwholesome state subject to clinging arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, one; in the case of the object condition, one … pe … in the case of the non-disappearance condition, one. (The Group on Clinging should be expanded in detail.
The Group on Clinging from the Wholesome Triplet is finished.
